text:
Alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection tweaks rolled last night we're seeing a steady KV cache memory growth on long-context workloads. +18% heap over 1M tokens on canary1, and a noticeable uptick in page churn. :frowning:
Maria: ugh. is this the kernel path that changed contiguous-block packing? any repro traces?
Cheng: repro attached (pprof snapshot + light trace). main thing I see: allocation pattern shifted to ~32B micro-chunks for KV entries when seq_len > 4k, so slab bins are much more fragmented. link: https://redwood.internal/r/PR-kernelexp (private)
Sam: that matches my local run. allocator ends up with lots of tiny free holes. eviction still works but compaction cost goes up because we scan many tiny slots. tail p99 up ~30ms on generation.
Priya: two quick ideas: (1) try increasing block granularity for long-context sessions (e.g., prefer 64B bins above threshold) and (2) background "mini-slab-aggregator" compactor that merges adjacent free micro-chunks into larger free blocks without moving live entries.
Alex: can you sketch the mini-slab-aggregator? sounds promising if it's non-blocking.
Priya: sketch below:
```
# mini-slab-aggregator heuristics (proto)
compact_cycle_ms = 500        # run every 500ms per core shard
max_merged_bytes = 64KB      # cap to avoid long work
age_bias = 0.6               # prefer older holes
reuse_hist_threshold = 1000  # if reuse histogram < threshold -> compact
# scoring: score = free_bytes * age_bias + (1/reuse_rate)*0.4 - fragmentation_penalty
```
Cheng: we can also use the KV access heatmap (per-key reuse count) to avoid compacting regions with cold-but-reused keys. i.e., don't merge holes near items with high reuse score.
Maria: need telemetry: show compacted_bytes, compaction_cycles, compaction_latency, p99 gen latency, paging_faults. also KV_PAGE_FAULT counter spiking in prod canary.
Sam: warning — compaction must be throttled during bursty traffic else it'll add tail latency. propose per-shard budget + yield after X ms OR after N merges.
Alex: agree. let's add a queue with budget tokens that refill slowly; compact only when queue >= cost.
Cheng: pasted a small eviction log snippet from canary1 showing the fault/evict pattern:
```
[2026-03-15T03:12:22Z] KV_EVICT: shard=7 evicted=128 live=10240 free_holes=342 frag_ratio=0.42
[2026-03-15T03:12:22Z] KV_PAGE_FAULT: shard=7 faults=312 recent_faults=47 paging_ms=12.4
[2026-03-15T03:12:22Z] COMPACT_SKIPPED: shard=7 reason="high_latency"
```
Priya: frag_ratio ~0.42 is pretty bad. if we can push it <0.25 we should see reclaim and lower paging. also consider adaptive block-size bumping for sessions that show long tail seq_lengths — treat them as "long-context lanes" with different binning.
Maria: would that affect model cache alignment or kernels? kernel-selection might assume certain KV layout to optimize KV-copy paths. need to confirm no regressions in kernel times.
Sam: good call — kernel fast paths expect aligned chunks; changing binning needs a compatibility layer so kernel doesn't get deoptimized. maybe maintain two views: compacted view (for allocator) + pinned layout for hot shards.
Alex: ops-bot just reported a canary OOM during a retry run — likely from compaction + sudden load.
ops-bot: Deploy Canary Canary-2026-03-15-07 failed on host gpu-32-11 with OOM (pid 9123). Logs: https://redwood.internal/logs/oom-9123
Priya: okay let's be conservative: 1) implement mini-slab-aggregator but disabled by default, 2) expose config flags: per-shard budget, max_merge_size, enable_long_context_binning, 3) run on canary with low budget and detailed telemetry.
Cheng: I'll draft the PR with the aggregator loop and metrics. can we add a perf test harness that runs 2M token long-context streams and measures frag_ratio + p99?
Maria: yes — add a smoke that verifies kernel hot path latency stays within 5% of baseline.
Sam: I'll add the per-shard token bucket and yield logic. also add an escape hatch flag to turn off compaction at runtime.
Alex: owners: Cheng (impl + perf test), Sam (scheduling + budget), Priya (heuristics + telemetry), Maria (canary + kernel regression checks). Let's aim for a canary next week. :thumbsup:
Priya: also adding a simple config example for QA to play with:
```json
{
  "mini_slab_aggregator": {
    "enabled": false,
    "cycle_ms": 500,
    "max_merged_bytes": 65536,
    "per_shard_budget_ms": 2,
    "age_bias": 0.6
  }
}
```
Alex: great. Cheng/ Sam/ Priya, pair up on the initial PR and ping me for a review. I'll schedule canary runs and watch the telemetry.
Maria: thanks — I'll wire dashboards for frag_ratio + KV_PAGE_FAULT + compaction metrics before canary.
Cheng: noted. starting draft now.
Sam: onboarded. will avoid doing compaction during warm-up window to reduce OOM risk.
Priya: cool. if we get quick wins we can do runtime tune (enable for only long-context lanes) before full rollout.
Alex: perfect. closing here, will follow up in the PR thread.
